subject: Pricing annex: variance protection + discount staircase (redline review)
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@praxisai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Praxis AI Procurement <procurement@praxisai.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Pricing annex: variance protection and discount staircase

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of clarifying questions on the pricing exhibit we received yesterday. The primary points are:

- We want a clear definition of the "variance protection" mechanism, specifically how the cap/floor interacts with quarterly true-ups.
- Praxis uses a blended compute forecast across regions; we need confirmation that the floor won't trigger clawbacks if usage shifts regionally within the commitment band.
- Our finance team also needs the discount staircase limits spelled out for year 1 vs year 2 (we typically ask for a maximum step-down of 7% per band).

Can you send a redline with proposed language that addresses regional shifting and clarifies whether the cap is applied on a per-region or consolidated basis? Also, procurement would prefer a mutual termination right if annual shortfall exceeds 40% of committed tokens.

Appreciate it — aiming to get this into our SOW review cycle next week.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Procurement, Praxis AI
[sarah.jenkins@praxisai.com]

--
Attachment: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@praxisai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing annex: variance protection and discount staircase

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a redline of the pricing annex with three focused changes we think will address Praxis's concerns:

1) Consolidated-floor approach: we propose language that applies the floor at the consolidated account level (all regions) to avoid regional churn triggering clawbacks, but keeps per-region caps to limit exposure in the case of concentrated spikes.

2) True-up cadence: quarterly measurement with an annual settlement and an annualized true-up window. This preserves predictability for both sides and avoids forced clawbacks mid-year.

3) Stair-step caps: we specified year-1 and year-2 maximum step-downs and included a hard ceiling of 10% on discount step-downs per-year (we kept your 7% ask in the comment for negotiation).

On mutual termination: we retained mutual termination on material shortfall but suggested 50% rather than 40% as a starting point; that's a negotiation lever we can move.

I've looped in Lauren and Neha for commercial and legal sign-off. If Praxis wants to trade the 40% mutual-termination ask for a slightly higher minimum floor (~65% of committed tokens instead of 60%), that could be an acceptable compromise from our side.

Attached: Praxis_Redwood_Pricing_Annex_Redline.pdf (redline, PDF)

Next steps I propose:
- You review the attached redline and mark any line edits.
- If acceptable, Neha will prepare a clean copy for signature and we can route via DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call if it's easier.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

--
Attachment: Praxis_Redwood_Pricing_Annex_Redline.pdf (PDF - redline)

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@praxisai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Praxis AI Procurement <procurement@praxisai.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T12:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing annex: variance protection and discount staircase

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear tradeoffs. A few inline notes from procurement/finance after reviewing the PDF:

> On consolidated-floor approach: we appreciate applying the floor at account level, but we still need a regional carveout for EU usage because our EU customers are priced differently and migrate more unpredictably. Can we make the EU floor measured separately if EU usage exceeds 30% of total?

Also: the mutual termination threshold at 50% is a non-starter for us; 40% is necessary given our purchasing governance. If Redwood needs to protect downside, we would accept a higher minimum floor (67%) but only if the mutual termination stays at 40%.

Procurement prefers no unilateral clawbacks; any adjustments should be mutually agreed in the annual true-up. Can Neha confirm whether the proposed per-region cap would allow us to access burst capacity without triggering penalties?

We're ready to proceed quickly once we have that EU carveout and a final redline reflecting the 40% mutual termination. DocuSign link to our internal PO will be sent after the annex is finalized.

Best,
Sarah

--
Attachment: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T15:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Pricing annex: variance protection and discount staircase — agreed negotiating position

Team — quick summary for legal/commercial ops:

- Praxis agrees to consolidated-floor but requires an EU carveout if EU >30% of usage. They insist on mutual termination at 40% shortfall. Their concession: they will accept a 67% minimum floor if we keep 40% mutual termination.
- They want explicit language that burst/buffer capacity for short-term spikes (<=14 days) is excluded from shortfall calculation.

Request: Neha, can you prepare a slim redline that: (1) implements an EU carveout threshold at 30%, (2) preserves the consolidated-floor otherwise, (3) codifies burst capacity exclusion (<=14 days), and (4) accepts mutual termination at 40% provided the minimum guaranteed floor is 67%?

If legal approves, Marissa/ I will send the clean exhibit and push DocuSign. I think this is an acceptable commercial outcome that avoids an escalated procurement loop.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Attachment: final_pricing_exhibit_v3.pdf (PDF - clean candidate for signature)
thread_summary: Negotiation on pricing annex redline for Praxis AI: Redwood offered consolidated floor, per-region caps, quarterly true-up, and stair-step limits. Praxis pushed for EU carveout and 40% mutual termination. Parties agreed on a compromise: accept 40% mutual termination if minimum floor set to 67% and burst usage (<=14 days) excluded from shortfall calculations. Legal to prepare final redline.
